source: Combined from two sources: (1) VVOB Cambodia / MAFF Kampong Thom GAP training presentation, Oct 5, 2010; (2) FAO-EU / MAFF rice production document, title and full source URL illegible due to poor scan quality — no elibrary URL confirmed
text: Both source documents agree on similar harvest timing guidance. Harvest is recommended when about 80-85% of grains in the field have turned golden/mature-colored, which is roughly 30-35 days after flowering. Before cutting, drain standing water from the field about 7-10 days ahead of harvest so the ground firms up and grain does not spoil in wet soil. At the panicle level, look for grains that feel firm and full rather than soft or shriveled; harvesting too early increases the share of chalky, broken, or unfilled grain, while harvesting too late increases shattering losses and can lower the quality and quantity of milled rice recovered. Cut rice is then left to dry in the field for roughly 2 days before threshing. After threshing, grain should be sun-dried on a mat or drying floor; target moisture for storage is around 12-14%, and farmers are advised to plan for about 2 full sunny days of drying to reach this level. Note: the 80-85% maturity and 12-14% storage-moisture figures are illustrative field targets used across both sources rather than exact laboratory values — actual timing should still be judged by visual grain condition in the field.
